reasoning: Squaring an odd-length permutation cycle preserves one cycle of that length, while squaring an even-length cycle produces two cycles of half its length. Consequently every even cycle length in the target permutation must occur an even number of times. This is also sufficient: take an internal square root for each odd cycle and interleave each pair of equal even cycles into one twice-long cycle. Count cycles, including fixed points, and check exactly this parity condition.
